value: A reconstructed prototype carrying one MORE trailing parameter than the retail function is INVISIBLE in the callee - a parameter that is never read emits no prologue code, so the callee can measure byte-EXACT at either arity and its own bytes can never settle the question - while every CALLER pays one or more instructions materialising the phantom argument. The tell is a caller residual of the shape `ours-only -1 <lwz|li|mr>` immediately around the call, with the target holding a value in the argument register that the aligned view shows serving some OTHER purpose (a nearby store). PROCEDURE when a call-site residual survives several argument spellings: stop respelling the argument and settle the arity from evidence OUTSIDE the callee - other call sites in the tree (a K&R `extern f(); ` declaration next to a three-argument call is the loudest), the Xbox PDB signature, and whether the callee ever reads the register. Measured on game/enemy/enemy::init_enemy: four argument spellings (field reload, literal, shared temporary, assignment-in-argument) all held the count at T136/O137, and dropping SetEnemyObj's 4th parameter - named `unused` in its own definition at src/game/game/gamemain.c:837, with a sibling call at src/game/enemy/enemy.c:5269 already passing three - took it to T136/O136 and real 27 -> 10 in one build, with gamemain.c::SetEnemyObj still measuring EXACT afterwards.
